findings.evidence: Printed p. 87: "one H100 sustains ~2,472 tok/s at 35% MFU". Printed p. 88: "the 8-GPU host needs ~0.47 s (9,200 ÷ 19,780 = 0.465 s; 19,780 = 8 × 2,472.5 tok/s)". Printed p. 88 again: "the host's capacity screen is the ~19,800 tok/s sustained-planning rate at 35% MFU".
findings.issue: The per-GPU sustained-planning prefill rate is quoted as ~2,472 tok/s on one page and 2,472.5 tok/s on the next; the corresponding host figure is ~19,800 tok/s in two places and 19,780 tok/s in the explicit 8 × 2,472.5 derivation. The exact value is 8 × 0.989e15 × 0.35 ÷ 140e9 = 19,780 tok/s; ~19,800 is the rounded form and 19,780 the exact form, but the text never says the 19,800 is the rounded presentation of 19,780, so a reader cross-checking the two occurrences sees a 20 tok/s discrepancy.
findings.fix_instruction: State the exact sustained-planning rate once (19,780 tok/s per host, 2,472.5 tok/s per GPU) and label the ~19,800 as its rounded presentation wherever the rounded form appears. Alternatively, use 19,780 consistently in the arithmetic and 19,800 only in prose, with a one-time parenthetical that the prose figure is rounded.

findings.evidence: "per-request API list cost falls from $0.01164 to ≈$0.0030 — the input leg goes from 9,200 × $1.20/1M = $0.01104 to 2,000 × $1.20/1M = $0.00240 while the output leg stays 300 × $2.00/1M = $0.0006, so the total moves $0.01164 → ≈$0.0030, a ~3.9× reduction ($0.01164 ÷ $0.0030 = 3.88)"
findings.issue: The arithmetic checks: $0.00240 + $0.0006 = $0.00300 ≈ $0.0030, and $0.01164 ÷ $0.0030 = 3.88. The text says '~3.9× reduction'. 3.88 rounds to 3.9 at one decimal. Correct. However, the original total $0.01164 = $0.01104 + $0.00060 = $0.01164 exactly, so the original is exact while the reduced is rounded to $0.0030 (from $0.00300). The ratio 0.01164/0.00300 = 3.88 exactly. All arithmetic verified correct — no defect.

50 × 8.6 = 430. 430/17 = 25.294... The ceiling of 25.29 is 26. Correct. Then: 'the u-only screen at a 70% target utilization the normative host-count form of Ch 17 Table 17-1 gives ⌈26 ÷ 0.70⌉ = ⌈37.14⌉ = 38 hosts (the occupancy cross-check ⌈430/(17 × 0.7)⌉ = ⌈430/11.9⌉ = ⌈36.13⌉ = 37 sits one host below it)'. Check: 26/0.70 = 37.14, ceiling = 38. Correct. 430/(17×0.7) = 430/11.9 = 36.13, ceiling = 37. Correct. Then: '⌈430/(17 × 0.70 × 0.95)⌉ = ⌈430/11.305⌉ = ⌈38.04⌉ = 39'. Check: 17×0.70×0.95 = 11.305. 430/11.305 = 38.036, ceiling = 39. Correct. Then: 'total (provisioned) = ⌈26 ÷ 0.665⌉ = ⌈39.10⌉ = 40 provisioned, 39 working'. Check: 0.70 × 0.95 = 0.665. 26/0.665 = 39.098, ceiling = 40. Correct. All arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "A prefill-throughput cross-check from the Chapter 8 model bounds it from below: 50 rps × 9,200 input = 460,000 prefill tokens/s ÷ ~19,800 tokens/s per host … = 24 hosts (460,000 ÷ 19,800 = 23.23, ceiled to a whole host)"
findings.issue: 460,000 / 19,800 = 23.232..., ceiling = 24. Correct. The text says '24 hosts'. However, 19,800 tok/s is itself stated as 8 × 2,472.5 = 19,780, printed as '~19,800'. Using the unrounded 19,780: 460,000/19,780 = 23.256, ceiling = 24. Same result. Using 19,800: 23.23, ceiling = 24. Same result. Arithmetic verified correct — no defect.

9,200/1,000,000 × 1.20 = 0.00920 × 1.20 = 0.01104. Correct. 300/1,000,000 × 2.00 = 0.00030 × 2.00 = 0.00060. Correct. Sum = 0.01104 + 0.00060 = 0.01164. Correct. The text rounds to ≈$0.012 (two significant figures of $0.01164). The rounding 0.01164 → 0.012 is a reasonable one-significant-figure rounding (0.01164 → 0.012 at two significant digits would be 0.012). Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "one host's 436 GB KV budget holds 436 ÷ 6.03 ≈ 72 slots instead of 17"
findings.issue: Check: a 2,000-input + 300-output slot = 2,300 tokens. 2,300 × 2,621,440 B = 6,029,312,000 B ≈ 6.03 GB. Correct. 436/6.03 = 72.31, floor to 72. Correct. The text says '≈ 72 slots'. Correct. But note: this uses the input-only token count (2,000) plus output (300) for the slot size, which is the resident basis (2,300 = 2,000 input + 300 output), consistent with the book's slot-counting convention. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "full-utilization hosts N = ⌈λ × W_exec ÷ 17 slots⌉ → ⌈86 ÷ 17⌉ = 6 at average and ⌈344 ÷ 17⌉ = 21 at peak"
findings.issue: 86/17 = 5.059, ceiling = 6. Correct. 344/17 = 20.24, ceiling = 21. Correct. Then: 'provisioned total = ⌈N ÷ (u × ρ)⌉ = ⌈N ÷ 0.665⌉, working = total − 1 → 6 hosts → ⌈6 ÷ 0.665⌉ = 10 provisioned, 9 working'. 6/0.665 = 9.02, ceiling = 10. Correct. '21 hosts → ⌈21 ÷ 0.665⌉ = 32 provisioned, 31 working'. 21/0.665 = 31.58, ceiling = 32. Correct. '10 × $14.6K ≈ $146K and 32 × $14.6K ≈ $467K'. 10 × 14.6 = 146. Correct. 32 × 14.6 = 467.2 ≈ 467. Correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "at the ~6-host average the whole-fleet spend is ~$120/hour (≈ $0.0333 per second), so ~92,000 / 0.0333 ≈ ~2.76 million input tokens per $1 of fleet spend"
findings.issue: 6 hosts × $20/hr = $120/hr. $120/3600 = $0.03333/s. 92,000/0.033333 = 2,760,000 ≈ 2.76M. Correct. And: '~3,000 / 0.0333 ≈ ~90,000 output tokens per $1'. 3,000/0.033333 = 90,000. Correct. The text then says '92,000 ÷ 0.0333 = 2,762,762 → ~2.76M at three significant figures'. 92,000/0.0333 = 2,762,762.7. Correct (using 0.0333 truncated). And '3,000 ÷ 0.0333 = 90,090 → ~90K at two, which is the precision the chapter prints'. 3,000/0.0333 = 90,090. Correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "on the wall-clock paid-occupancy basis (the sidebar's $87,600/mo — the fleet paid for all 730 h/mo, divided by the same 6.24M active-hours requests) it is ≈$14.04 per 1K, i.e. ~$0.014 per request. The 4.2× gap between $0.0033 and $0.014 is the duty cycle (730 ÷ 173.33 = 4.21)"

"Canonical Workload — the single reference set. This box is the one authoritative set of numbers every chapter disciplines on. When a chapter states a workload parameter, it comes from here and nowhere else."
findings.issue: This box (p.66) contains a 'Mean request service time (planning headline)' row with value '~10 s [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]'. The box explicitly states this is 'NOT the W used in any Little's-law occupancy computation' and that the occupancy service time is 'the derived W_exec = prefill + decode ≈ 8.58 s'. The box also contains 'Execution occupancy ~86 requests at 10 rps; ~344 at 40 rps' derived with W_exec ≈ 8.6 s. Both values coexist in the same box with explicit disambiguation. The box is internally consistent and well-labeled. Verified correct — no defect.

findings.evidence: "the figure's ~23 GB label" and "per-token read traffic ... is 12.8B × 2 bytes = 25.6 GB"
findings.issue: In the Figure 3.4 caption discussion, the text says 'Inside that resident total the two selected experts hold 2 × 11.4 GB = 22.8 GB, the figure's ~23 GB label.' Then: 'Per-token read traffic — what the memory bus moves for one batch-1 decode token — is 12.8B × 2 bytes = 25.6 GB.' Check: 2 × 11.4 = 22.8. 12.8 × 2 = 25.6. The text then says 25.6 GB 'is those same 22.8 GB plus those same ~2.8 GB' — but 22.8 + 2.8 = 25.6. And 1.4B × 2 = 2.8 GB. So 11.4B + 1.4B = 12.8B active, and (11.4 + 1.4) × 2 = 12.8 × 2 = 25.6. The decomposition 22.8 + 2.8 = 25.6 is correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "On a single 8×H100 host at the same 40 rps peak, prefill demand is ~18.6× that host's sustained capacity — Ch 8 §3, Table 8-1"
findings.issue: 40 × 1.29 PFLOP = 51.6 PFLOP/s. Host capacity at 35% MFU = 8 × 0.989 × 0.35 = 2.769 PFLOP/s. 51.6/2.769 = 18.64 ≈ 18.6×. Correct. This same 18.6× figure appears in Ch 6 p.158 ('~18.6 host-equivalents') and is consistent. Arithmetic verified and cross-references consistent — no defect.

findings.evidence: "the queue is unbounded and p95 TTFT grows until admission control intervenes; the 2.5 s figure does not describe that case"
findings.issue: On p.126 (Ch 6), the text says 'p95 TTFT drifts to ~2.5 s [canonical scenario][DERIVED]: 1.0 s + one full 1.08 s prefill ≈ 2.1 s, and part of a second prefill on top of that ≈ 2.5 s.' Then on p.100 (Ch 6 continuation) the text adds the fleet scope note: 'On a single 8×H100 host at the same 40 rps peak, prefill demand is ~18.6× that host's sustained capacity — Ch 8 §3, Table 8-1 — so the queue is unbounded and p95 TTFT grows until admission control intervenes; the 2.5 s figure does not describe that case.' The 2.5 s derivation: 1.0 + 1.08 = 2.08 ≈ 2.1, plus 'part of a second prefill' — 2.1 + 0.4 = 2.5. This is approximate and the text presents it as a rough illustration, not precise arithmetic. The labeling [canonical scenario][DERIVED] is appropriate for an illustrative derivation from canonical inputs. However, the derivation 'part of a second prefill on top of that ≈ 2.5 s' does not specify what fraction of the second prefill, making the 2.5 value unreproducible from stated inputs alone. For a [DERIVED] label, the derivation should be reproducible.
findings.fix_instruction: Either specify the fraction of the second prefill that completes (e.g. '≈0.4 s of a second prefill') so 1.0 + 1.08 + 0.4 = 2.48 ≈ 2.5, or relabel as [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] since the 2.5 s is chosen to illustrate queueing rather than derived from a complete calculation.
